title: Chris King Re-Enters the BMX Hub Game
content:
The gate is about to drop on Chris King’s next big thing. Just in time for the MADE custom bike show, Chris King Precision Components is releasing redesigned, lightweight, race-focused, BMX disc hubs.

“We last made BMX hubs in 2018,” said King president and General Manager Kirby Bedsaul, “and not a day has passed since then without riders asking us to make them again, so we’re happy, finally, to be able to get those riders going on something new, an improvement on the old design, and a hubset we think will win a lot of races for those riders who have been patiently waiting for this day.”

Chris King BMX Hubs Quick Hits

  • Price:
    • rear hub: $580
    • front hub: $310
  • Titanium axle bolts are $35/pair
  • Weight:
    • rear hub: 297g
    • front hub: 170g.
  • Front hub available in 20mm axle
  • Rear hub available in 15mm thru-axle or M10 bolt-on
  • Compatible with 72t or 36t Ring Drive

The front, with no rotor mount, is made for 20mm axles. The rear has a 6-bolt rotor mount, and incorporates the legendary King RingDrive™ with internal needle bearing, just like the King BMX hubs of yore. The rear hub is available for 15mm thru-axle or M10 bolt-on. The new BMX hubsets will be available in all colors. The rear hub will come stock with King’s 72T RingDrive for quickest engagement but is also compatible with their 36T RingDrive for lower drag and higher maximum speed.

“These hubs are really race-optimized,” Bedsaul continued. “We reduced rear hub weight by about 50g, while maintaining stiffness with a one-piece hardened stainless steel axle. We increased the flange diameter and optimized flange angles for 20″ rims. You combine all that with the tuneability our hubs offer, and these new hubs should make BMX racers very excited.”

The bolt-on version of the rear hub comes with steel bolts, though riders can also order custom Ti bolts (finished like King’s Robert Axle Project axles) to upgrade their hubset for maximum weight savings. All hubsets are available in 36-hole configuration.

Find out more at Chris King.
